The process description represents the Carbon Capture system designed for the processing of the conditioned BFG. The CO Island 2 is mainly comprised of an Absorber, a Stripper, CO conditioning equipment (Compressor, Dehydrator, 2 Supercritical Condensers, and Supercritical CO Pumps), process heat exchangers, and solvent management 2 Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 11 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 systems (Filter Pump, Filtration Systems, Solvent Make-Up, and Electrodialysis Reclaimer). The BFG enters the Carbon Capture Island at the Absorber, where the ION solvent selectively absorbs CO via an 2 exothermic, reversible reaction. An Absorber Cooler between the two CO absorption beds lowers the 2 solvent temperature for optimal CO absorption. A two-stage water wash above the CO absorption zone 2 2 recovers practically all solvent vapors and maintains overall water balance. The lean solvent is introduced at the top of the Contactor zone of the Absorber 2 and flows down through the first section of packing. The contact with the solvent removes about 95% of the CO at full load via an exothermic, reversible reaction. With the high concentration of CO in this gas, 2 2 the exothermic reaction of capturing CO with the solvent quickly raises the solvent temperature to levels 2 that drastically reduce the ability to capture CO further. The solvent then flows to the base of the Absorber, 2 where it is held in a sump for further circulation to the Stripper. The lower water wash LWW consists of a process water loop that first contacts the BFG in Absorber to recover solvent at intermediate temperatures. The UWW consists of a process water loop that circulates through Absorber packing. The process water collects in a reservoir at the base of the Structured Packing and flows into the UWW Surge Vessel. The process water is pumped through the UWW Coolers and then returned to the UWW Absorber Packing; the outlet temperature from the UWW Coolers fluctuates over a small range to control the UWW Surge Vessel level through water condensation from the BFG.
